gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-onest: Onest reads as a line gliding under the eye like wire, with short ascenders above big bowls. Onest also lets Stencilia, the structural display heading, do the striking, since its sans-serif strokes never pool ink at the turns.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-open-sans: Structural and striking up top, with Stencilia's spacious curve gaps. Open Sans sits beneath as a smooth sans-serif with bulky lowercase proportions and no clogged curves, a sturdier, softer presence than the heading.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-orienta: Modern in feel, Orienta lets its counters breathe like a hollow reed. Stencilia handles the structure above, and the plain sans below keeps its capitals and lowercase close in height.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-oxygen: Oxygen reads as a sans-serif whose curves never close back on themselves, with lowercase nearly matching its capitals. Stencilia's structure can stay up top, so text could sit modestly smaller.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-parkinsans: Contemporary lines lead here, with Stencilia's spacious terminals and compact upper gap giving it structure. And Parkinsans, a plain sans with wide-mouthed letters, stays crisp even when you shrink its size.
